env.name: cmv
env.description:
2,000 Reddit r/ChangeMyView discussions (balanced). One row = one post with its counter-argument comments.
Columns:
  - post_created_utc: Unix timestamp of the original post (no comment times).
  - title: the original poster's (OP) post heading / claim statement.
  - argument: the OP's explanation of their view (the post body). May contain quotes and marked edits.
  - OC_comments: JSON-encoded list of counter-argument comments written by OTHER users (not the OP).
    List order is not rank or chronology. Row-level measures must say whether they mean any comment,
    all comments, an average, or a count.
  - conversation: formatted discussion text overlapping OC_comments; may include later replies and
    explicit view-change announcements (outcome leakage) — avoid unless interaction is required.
  - log_length: supplied log-transformed length measure (undocumented construction).
  - post_score: the original post's observed Reddit score at collection.
  - delta: OUTCOME, 1 if the OP changed their view, else 0. Never a predictor.
  - post_id, comment_id: identifiers, never predictors.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument includes explicit comparisons to established scientific or historical norms are associated with lower view change than those without such comparisons.

features.name: op_explicit_comparison_to_established_norms
features.definition: OP's own argument text (title for context): 1 if it explicitly compares the view/subject to an established scientific or historical norm, else 0
features.spec: Read the OP's argument (body), using title only to identify the OP's claim. Output 1 if the OP's own text explicitly compares the subject of their view to an established scientific norm (e.g., accepted scientific consensus, laws/standards of science, established empirical findings) or an established historical norm (e.g., historical precedent, long-standing historical practice or standard), stating a similarity, difference, or conformity/deviation relative to that norm. A mere passing mention of science or history without a comparison, and comparisons to non-scientific/non-historical things (personal anecdotes, current everyday norms) give 0. Exclude quoted text that is from others and not adopted by OP, and edits that merely report replies. Output 0 if the argument is assessable and has no such comparison. Output null if argument is missing or empty/unparseable.

decomposed.h0: Mean delta (view change) does not differ between discussions whose OP argument has op_explicit_comparison_to_established_norms=1 and those with 0.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with op_explicit_comparison_to_established_norms=1 have lower view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Argument may contain later edits; no initial snapshot is assumed. "Established norms" is semantic with no fixed list. OLS on binary outcome (linear probability model).

decomposed.hypothesis: Arguments expressing explicit fear of social rejection or isolation are associated with lower view-change rates than arguments stating beliefs without emotional self-defense.

features.name: op_explicit_fear_social_rejection
features.definition: OP's own title and argument text (excluding quoted others, and edits only if not OP's own): 1 if OP explicitly expresses fear of social rejection, ostracism, or isolation, else 0
features.spec: Read title and argument together. Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly states fear/worry/anxiety of being rejected, ostracized, judged into exclusion, abandoned, or isolated by others (e.g. 'I'm afraid my friends will stop talking to me if I hold this view'). Fear must be explicit and about social rejection/isolation, not merely disagreement, topic discussion, or fear of non-social harms. Ignore quoted text from others or reported opponents' positions unless OP adopts it. Return 0 if the text is assessable and has no such expression. Return null if title and argument are both missing or empty/unparseable.

features.name: op_belief_without_emotional_self_defense
features.definition: OP's own title and argument text: 1 if OP states their belief/reasoning with no emotional self-defense (no fear, hurt, defensiveness, pleading for protection or justification against anticipated judgment), else 0
features.spec: Read title and argument together. Return 1 if the OP states their view and reasons in a plain way containing no emotional self-defense: no expressed fear of rejection/isolation, no anxiety about being judged, no defensive preemptive justification driven by emotion, no pleas for sympathy or protection of self. Mere neutral or mildly emotive wording about the topic does not count as self-defense. Return 0 if any such emotional self-defense is present (including fear of social rejection). Ignore quoted others unless adopted by OP. Return null if both fields are missing or empty.

decomposed.h0: View-change rate does not differ between posts with op_explicit_fear_social_rejection=1 and posts with op_belief_without_emotional_self_defense=1.
decomposed.h1: Posts with op_explicit_fear_social_rejection=1 have a lower view-change rate than posts with op_belief_without_emotional_self_defense=1.
decomposed.note: The claim contrasts fear-of-rejection arguments with plain-belief arguments. In the proposed regression the fear coefficient is relative to a omitted residual group (other emotional self-defense without fear, or neither), not relative to the plain group, so no single coefficient equals the claimed contrast (it would need beta_fear - beta_plain). Hence term=null. Subsetting to the two groups is not expressible in the rhs. Fear is probably rare, so power is limited. The hypothesis does not say whether the comparison is adjusted for anything; no controls were added.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments that cite specific, functioning institutional precedents are associated with a higher probability of view change than those relying on abstract normative principles.

features.name: any_comment_cites_functioning_institutional_precedent
features.definition: Any OC comment: 1 if at least one comment cites a specific, identifiable institutional precedent presented as functioning/working in practice.
features.spec: Read the OC_comments JSON list (order not meaningful). Return 1 if at least one comment cites a specific, identifiable institutional precedent (e.g., a named country's law, policy, court system, organization or program) and presents it as having worked or functioning in practice, as evidence for the commenter's point. Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none do so; vague generalities, hypotheticals, purely abstract principles, or precedents shown as failed do not count. Endorsement by the OP is not required. Text the commenter merely quotes from others does not count unless adopted. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable or empty. Do not use conversation or delta.

features.name: any_comment_relies_on_abstract_normative_principle
features.definition: Any OC comment: 1 if at least one comment relies on an abstract normative principle (general moral/ethical/value principle) as its argument basis.
features.spec: Read the OC_comments JSON list (order not meaningful). Return 1 if at least one comment's argument relies on an abstract normative principle (e.g., general claims about rights, fairness, justice, what ought to be, stated as principle) rather than on a specific concrete example or precedent. Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none do so. A comment that mainly rests on a specific precedent does not count merely for mentioning a value word. Quoted text from others does not count unless adopted. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable or empty. Do not use conversation or delta.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_cites_functioning_institutional_precedent has no association with view change probability relative to any_comment_relies_on_abstract_normative_principle (equal coefficients).
decomposed.h1: Rows with any_comment_cites_functioning_institutional_precedent have higher view-change probability than rows with any_comment_relies_on_abstract_normative_principle (coefficient of precedent greater than that of abstract principle).
decomposed.note: The claim is a contrast between precedent-citing and abstract-principle comments (beta_A - beta_B), which no single design-matrix coefficient represents, so term is null. Features are row-level any-indicators and can overlap; comment-level comparison is unavailable. Row-level association only; comments are unordered.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring longer precomputed log-transformed discussion length are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: log_length_supplied
features.definition: Supplied log_length column: the precomputed log-transformed discussion length value for the row, unchanged
features.spec: df['log_length'] as float. Observed range about 0.69 to 7.44, no missing in the data. Return null if missing or non-numeric. Construction of the column is undocumented; do not recompute or rescale it.

decomposed.h0: log_length_supplied has zero association with the likelihood of the OP changing their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Higher log_length_supplied is associated with a higher likelihood of the OP changing their view.
decomposed.note: log_length construction is undocumented (it is unclear whether it measures the OP post, the comments, or the full conversation). The claim is tested as a linear association with the supplied value. OLS on the binary outcome is a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains explicit admissions of uncertainty are associated with a higher probability of view change than those asserting absolute certainty.

features.name: op_explicit_uncertainty
features.definition: OP's own argument text: 1 if the OP explicitly admits uncertainty or possible error about their own view/claims, else 0.
features.spec: Read only the argument column (OP post body; may contain later edits, which are not separated out; do not infer an initial version). Return 1 if the OP in their own voice explicitly expresses uncertainty, doubt, or admits they might be wrong about their view or claims (e.g. 'I may be wrong', 'I'm not sure', 'I could be missing something'). Exclude quoted external text, opponents' positions reported by the OP, and generic invitations to respond ('change my view') or hedging of minor details unrelated to doubt about the OP's position. Return 0 if the text is assessable and has no such explicit statement. Return null if argument is missing or empty/unparseable.

features.name: op_asserts_absolute_certainty
features.definition: OP's own argument text: 1 if the OP explicitly asserts absolute certainty about their view (e.g. cannot be wrong, no possible counterargument), else 0.
features.spec: Read only the argument column (OP post body; later edits not separable). Return 1 if the OP in their own voice explicitly asserts absolute certainty or incontrovertibility of their view (e.g. 'there is no possible counterargument', 'I am 100% certain', 'undeniably', 'I can't be wrong'). Ordinary confident opinion statements without explicit absolute-certainty claims give 0. Exclude quoted external text and reported opponents' positions. This is not the complement of explicit uncertainty: a post can be 0 on both. Return null if argument is missing or empty/unparseable.

decomposed.h0: Posts with op_explicit_uncertainty=1 have the same probability of view change as posts with op_asserts_absolute_certainty=1.
decomposed.h1: Posts with op_explicit_uncertainty=1 have a higher probability of view change than posts with op_asserts_absolute_certainty=1.
decomposed.note: The claim contrasts uncertainty vs absolute certainty, i.e. beta_uncertainty - beta_certainty, relative to a neither-group baseline; no single design-matrix coefficient represents this, so term is null (a linear-combination test would be needed). The two indicators are not complements. The argument may include later edits; no initial snapshot is inferred. Outcome is delta (added automatically).

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments frequently challenging multiple distinct factual premises within the argument are positively associated with view change.

features.name: distinct_factual_premises_challenged_count
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments, not OP) read against the OP title/argument: number of distinct factual premises of the OP's argument that are challenged by at least one comment
features.spec: Read title, argument and OC_comments jointly. Identify the distinct factual (empirical/descriptive, not value, logical-structure or definitional) premises stated in the OP's title/argument. Count how many distinct such premises are explicitly challenged (disputed as false, unsupported, or inaccurate with factual argument) by at least one comment in OC_comments. Count each premise once even if several comments challenge it; do not count the same premise twice for rewordings. Do not count challenges to values, reasoning, or conclusions only, nor agreement, concessions, or comments challenging things the OP did not claim. Ignore the OP's later edits only if clearly marked as edits; do not use conversation. Output a non-negative integer (0 = comments assessable and none challenge a factual premise). Null if OC_comments is empty/unparseable or argument is missing.

features.name: multiple_factual_premises_challenged
features.definition: Derived: 1 if at least two distinct factual premises of the OP argument are challenged by the counter-arguments, else 0
features.spec: Python: None if distinct_factual_premises_challenged_count is null, else int(distinct_factual_premises_challenged_count >= 2). Based on the prompt feature distinct_factual_premises_challenged_count (reads title, argument, OC_comments).

decomposed.h0: multiple_factual_premises_challenged has no positive association with delta (coefficient <= 0).
decomposed.h1: multiple_factual_premises_challenged is positively associated with delta (coefficient > 0).
decomposed.note: "Frequently" has no specified frequency cutoff; operationalized only as challenges to at least two distinct factual premises across the row's comments (the "multiple" threshold), not a per-comment frequency. OC_comments is unordered and may be a subset of the discussion; the count aggregates over all comments. The argument may contain later edits. The binary is the tested term; the count is retained as the base measurement.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains fewer counter-argument responses are associated with a lower likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: oc_comment_count
features.definition: Row's OC_comments list: number of counter-argument comments (list length)
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list. Output len(list) as a non-negative integer. If the value is missing or unparseable as a JSON list, output null. An empty list gives 0. Count every element as one comment; no semantic deduplication.

decomposed.h0: oc_comment_count has no association with the likelihood of OP view change (coefficient = 0).
decomposed.h1: Higher oc_comment_count (more counter-argument comments) is associated with a higher likelihood of OP view change, so fewer comments means lower likelihood (coefficient > 0).
decomposed.note: The hypothesis says the "original argument contains" the counter-argument responses. The argument is the OP's post body, so this was read as the number of counter-argument comments in the discussion (OC_comments). "Fewer" has no stated cutoff, so the count is used as is. The count is the length of the supplied list. The list may be a sample, and the data may select which comments were kept. The outcome is binary but is modelled with OLS (a linear probability model). In the data seen, the count ranges from 1 to 17 with a median of 1.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions with at least three distinct counter-arguments in the posted comments are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: distinct_counterargument_count
features.definition: Other users' comments in OC_comments: number of distinct counter-arguments (semantically distinct challenges to the OP's view) posted across the comments
features.spec: Read title and argument (for the OP's claim) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than OP; order carries no meaning). Count the distinct counter-arguments against the OP's view across all comments: each separate line of reasoning/challenge counts once; the same argument repeated in several comments or restated within a comment counts once; comments that are not counter-arguments (agreement, jokes, questions only, moderator/bot notices, pure clarification) count zero. Do not use the conversation column or later replies. Output a non-negative integer. 0 if the list is valid but empty or has no counter-arguments. Null if OC_comments is missing or unparseable.

features.name: has_three_or_more_distinct_counterarguments
features.definition: Other users' comments in OC_comments: 1 if distinct_counterargument_count >= 3, else 0
features.spec: Using distinct_counterargument_count: return null if it is null; else int(distinct_counterargument_count >= 3).

decomposed.h0: Discussions with has_three_or_more_distinct_counterarguments = 1 have the same likelihood of OP view change as those with 0.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with has_three_or_more_distinct_counterarguments = 1 have a higher likelihood of OP view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: OC_comments is only the supplied sample of counter-argument comments, not necessarily all comments, and order/time is unknown. Distinct-argument counting is a semantic judgment. Outcome is binary; OLS gives a linear probability model. Threshold of three is taken from the claim.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original post title uses absolute certainty markers are associated with a lower likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: title_absolute_certainty
features.definition: OP post title: 1 if the title itself uses an absolute certainty marker (e.g., always, never, all, none, no one, definitely, certainly, undeniably, obviously, impossible, absolutely, 100%), else 0
features.spec: Read only the title column (the OP's claim heading; ignore the 'CMV:' prefix). Return 1 if the title's own wording asserts its claim with absolute certainty markers: universal/total quantifiers or frequency terms (always, never, all, every, none, no one, nothing), certainty/necessity terms (definitely, certainly, undeniably, obviously, absolutely, without doubt, impossible, 100%), or equivalent absolute phrasing. Return 0 if no such marker appears, including hedged or merely strong/opinionated wording (e.g., 'almost always', 'should', 'more', 'generally'), or when a marker is only mentioned in a negated/hedging sense (e.g., 'no reason to believe, with certainty' is judged by whether the title asserts absolute certainty itself). Judge the title alone, not body or comments. Empty or missing title: null.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with title_absolute_certainty = 1 have the same likelihood of OP view change (delta) as those with 0.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with title_absolute_certainty = 1 have a lower likelihood of OP view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Absolute certainty markers are an operational lexical/semantic judgment with no validated list. OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model. Only title is read.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where original posts explicitly invite critique or use tentative language are associated with higher view-change rates than those using absolute, definitive declarations.

features.name: op_invites_critique_or_tentative
features.definition: OP's own title and argument text (excluding quoted external text and marked edits' later additions where identifiable): 1 if the OP explicitly invites critique/challenge or uses explicitly tentative/hedged language about their own view
features.spec: Read title and argument together. Judge only the OP's own voice; ignore quotations of others and bot/moderator notices. Return 1 if the OP explicitly invites critique, counterarguments or being changed (e.g. 'change my view', 'tell me why I'm wrong', 'I may be wrong') beyond the bare 'CMV:' title prefix, or explicitly hedges their own stance with tentative wording (e.g. 'I think maybe', 'I'm not sure', 'it seems to me', 'I could be mistaken'). Return 0 if neither is present in assessable text. Null if title and argument are both missing or unreadable. Do not use text from edits as evidence of the initial post; argument may contain later edits, so treat all argument text as current text only. Do not treat absolute certainty as the complement of this feature.

features.name: op_absolute_definitive_declaration
features.definition: OP's own title and argument text: 1 if the OP states their view as an absolute, definitive, unqualified declaration (e.g. 'always', 'never', 'obviously', 'undeniably', 'there is no possible')
features.spec: Read title and argument together. Judge only the OP's own voice; ignore quotations of others and bot/moderator notices. Return 1 if the OP presents their central view as absolute or definitive, with categorical/universal wording or explicit certainty and no hedging of that central claim. Return 0 if the central view is hedged, qualified or not stated categorically. Null if both title and argument are missing or unreadable. This is not simply the absence of invitation or tentativeness; a post can be neither. Argument may contain later edits; treat as current text only.

decomposed.h0: View-change rate for posts with op_invites_critique_or_tentative=1 equals that for posts with op_absolute_definitive_declaration=1.
decomposed.h1: View-change rate is higher for posts with op_invites_critique_or_tentative=1 than for posts with op_absolute_definitive_declaration=1.
decomposed.note: The claim contrasts two named groups (invite/tentative vs absolute), i.e. beta_A - beta_B, which is not a single coefficient in the rhs; each coefficient is relative to posts with neither feature (and the overlap is allowed), so no single term represents the claim. A linear-combination test would be needed. Edits in argument may postdate the initial post; no initial snapshot is available. 'CMV:' prefix is excluded as a generic invitation.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring counter-arguments that explicitly cite specific real-world examples are associated with higher likelihood of original view change.

features.name: any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example
features.definition: Counter-argument comments in OC_comments (not OP): 1 if any comment explicitly cites at least one specific real-world example, else 0
features.spec: Read the OC_comments JSON list (each element is one counter-argument comment by a user other than the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly cites a specific, real-world example (a named or clearly identifiable real event, person, organization, place, study, product, historical case, or concrete real instance) used in the comment's argument. Generic hypotheticals, vague generalities ('some people', 'many countries'), invented scenarios, and mere topic mentions do not count. Endorsement is not needed; the comment itself must present the example. Return 0 if the list is parseable and non-empty and no comment does so. Return 0 for a valid empty list; null if OC_comments is missing or unparseable. Do not use conversation or any outcome.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example is unrelated to the probability of OP view change (coefficient = 0).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example = 1 have higher probability of OP view change than those with 0 (coefficient > 0).
decomposed.note: Linear probability model on binary delta. "Discussions featuring" interpreted as any comment citing an example; no frequency cutoff was specified. Association only, no controls. OC_comments order carries no chronology.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counterarguments containing measured, logical reasoning are positively associated with the original poster changing their mind compared to those containing emotional aggression in ChangeMyView discussions.

features.name: any_comment_measured_logical_reasoning
features.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: contains calm, measured, logically structured reasoning (1) vs none does (0)
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP; order carries no meaning). Return 1 if at least one comment presents measured, logical reasoning: a calm, civil tone with explicit premises, evidence or inference steps supporting a conclusion against the OP's view. Merely polite or merely civil comments without reasoning, and reasoning that is accompanied by hostile attacks do not count for that comment. Ignore quoted text from others unless the commenter adopts it. Return 0 if the list is parseable and no comment qualifies. Return null if OC_comments is missing/unparseable; an empty list gives null as there is nothing to assess.

features.name: any_comment_emotional_aggression
features.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: expresses emotional aggression (hostility, insults, contempt, angry/attacking language toward the OP or others) (1) vs none does (0)
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP; order carries no meaning). Return 1 if at least one comment itself expresses emotional aggression: insults, personal attacks, hostile or contemptuous language, angry outbursts or hostile sarcasm. Generic emotional wording, passion, or blunt disagreement without hostility does not count. Quoted text from others does not count unless the commenter adopts it. Return 0 if the list is parseable and no comment qualifies. Return null if OC_comments is missing/unparseable or empty.

decomposed.h0: Having any comment with measured logical reasoning versus any comment with emotional aggression (any_comment_measured_logical_reasoning vs any_comment_emotional_aggression) has equal association with the OP changing their view.
decomposed.h1: any_comment_measured_logical_reasoning has a larger positive association with delta than any_comment_emotional_aggression (beta_logical > beta_aggression).
decomposed.note: The claim is a contrast (logical vs aggressive), i.e. beta_logical - beta_aggression, which is not a single design-matrix coefficient in this specification, so no single term is testable without a linear-contrast test. Features are row-level any-comment indicators; the data lack per-comment outcome linkage (delta is per post, and the comments are not tied to which persuaded the OP). Comments may be both, or neither; overlap is allowed. No frequency cutoff is given by the hypothesis.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly quote and refute specific factual claims in the original post are associated with higher rates of view change.

features.name: quotes_and_refutes_op_factual_claim
features.definition: Any counter-argument comment (OC_comments): explicitly quotes or directly cites a specific factual claim from the OP's title/argument AND refutes that factual claim.
features.spec: Read title, argument and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP) jointly. Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly quotes (verbatim or a clear close quotation/block quote) a specific factual claim stated in the OP's title or argument and then disputes/refutes that factual claim (e.g. with counter-evidence or reasoning showing it is false or wrong). Merely mentioning the OP's topic, quoting a value judgment/opinion rather than a factual claim, quoting without refuting, or refuting without quoting gives no credit. The OP argument context is required to verify the quoted text and that it is a factual claim. List order is not chronology; ignore the conversation column. Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none qualifies. Return null if OC_comments is missing/unparseable or title and argument are both missing; an empty comment list gives null.

decomposed.h0: Rates of view change (delta) do not differ by quotes_and_refutes_op_factual_claim.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with quotes_and_refutes_op_factual_claim = 1 have a higher rate of view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Linear probability model on binary delta. "Specific factual claims" is judged semantically; the comparison is with discussions lacking such quote-and-refute. Association only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly validate the original poster's personal dignity or effort before introducing corrective logic are associated with higher view-change rates than purely logical refutations.

features.name: validates_op_dignity_or_effort_before_correction
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments, not OP): 1 if any comment explicitly validates the OP's personal dignity, worth, or effort before introducing its corrective argument within that comment
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users; order is not chronology), with title and argument as context for the OP. Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly affirms the OP's personal dignity, worth, or effort (e.g. praising their effort, acknowledging their struggle or hard work as valid/respectable, affirming them as a person) AND this validation appears earlier in that same comment than its corrective/counter logic. Generic politeness, thanks, agreement with a point, or praise of the argument's logic alone do not count; the validation must be about the OP personally or their effort. Do not use the conversation column or any later replies. Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none qualifies. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable, or empty.

features.name: purely_logical_refutation_only
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments, not OP): 1 if every comment is a corrective/counter-argument and none contains explicit validation of the OP's personal dignity or effort
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list by other users; order not meaningful) with title and argument as OP context. Return 1 if all comments consist of logical/factual counter-argument or refutation of the OP's view and no comment contains any explicit validation of the OP's personal dignity, worth, or effort (generic politeness or acknowledging a point's logic is not validation). Return 0 if any comment explicitly validates the OP personally or their effort, or if some comment is not a corrective argument at all (e.g. only a question or joke). Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable, or empty. Do not use the conversation column.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with validates_op_dignity_or_effort_before_correction = 1 have the same view-change rate as purely_logical_refutation_only = 1 discussions.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with validates_op_dignity_or_effort_before_correction = 1 have a higher view-change rate than purely_logical_refutation_only = 1 discussions.
decomposed.note: The claim contrasts validate-first versus purely logical discussions. In the joint model each coefficient is relative to the residual group (neither feature = 1), so no single coefficient equals the claimed contrast; the validation-minus-logical difference would need a linear contrast, so term is null. The validation feature is per row and any-comment, and comment order or chronology is unavailable. The 'before' ordering is judged within a single comment only. The conversation column is excluded because it leaks the outcome.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring counter-arguments that provide concrete real-world examples are associated with a higher likelihood of view change than those relying primarily on abstract reasoning.

features.name: any_comment_concrete_real_world_example
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments, any comment): 1 if at least one comment itself provides a concrete real-world example, else 0
features.spec: Read the OC_comments JSON list (comments by users other than the OP; order carries no meaning). Return 1 if at least one comment, in its own text, offers a specific concrete real-world example, case, instance, or named/identifiable real situation (e.g. a particular event, person, organization, product, law, study, or personal real-life anecdote) used to support its counter-argument. Return 0 if comments are assessable and none do so (purely abstract reasoning, hypotheticals, generic statements, or only definitions/principles). Do not count examples only appearing inside quoted OP text. Hypothetical invented scenarios do not count. Do not use conversation, delta, or later replies. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable, or empty list.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with any_comment_concrete_real_world_example=1 have the same likelihood of view change as those with 0.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_concrete_real_world_example=1 have a higher likelihood of view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: The claim contrasts concrete examples with discussions 'relying primarily on abstract reasoning'; the feature's 0 group is no concrete example in any comment, which approximates but is not identical to primarily abstract. 'Featuring' is operationalized as any comment, with no frequency cutoff. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly engage with the specific examples or premises cited in the original argument text are associated with a higher likelihood of view change.

features.name: any_comment_engages_op_examples_or_premises
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments) vs OP title+argument: 1 if any comment explicitly engages a specific example or premise cited in the OP's argument text, else 0
features.spec: Read title, argument (OP text; may contain later edits, treat as given) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users; order carries no meaning) jointly. Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly engages with a specific example or premise stated in the OP's argument (e.g. quotes/paraphrases it and responds, rebuts, questions, accepts, or analyzes that particular example/premise). Merely addressing the general topic or the title claim without reference to a specific example/premise from the argument is 0. Endorsement not required. Do not use the conversation column. Return 0 if comments are parseable and none qualify. Return null if OC_comments is missing/unparseable or argument is missing/empty. An empty comment list gives 0 if argument is present.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_engages_op_examples_or_premises has no association with the likelihood of view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Rows with any_comment_engages_op_examples_or_premises=1 have a higher likelihood of view change than rows with 0.
decomposed.note: Hypothesis says "counter-arguments" without specifying any/all/share; "any comment" is chosen operationally. Argument may include later edits; no initial snapshot is available. OLS on binary outcome is a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring counter-arguments that introduce concrete, personal labor-process details are associated with higher view-change rates than those relying solely on abstract normative principles.

features.name: any_comment_personal_labor_process_detail
features.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: introduces concrete, personal (first-hand or specific-person) details of how work/labor is actually done (tasks, workflow, conditions, procedures)
features.spec: Read the JSON list in OC_comments (comments by users other than OP; order carries no meaning). Return 1 if at least one comment itself introduces concrete labor-process details drawn from personal experience (the commenter's or a specific named/described person's job), e.g. specific tasks, workflow steps, shifts, tools, conditions, or procedures of actual work. Generic abstract statements about work, hypothetical examples without specific process detail, and quoted OP text do not count. Return 0 if the list is parsed and no comment does so. Return null if OC_comments is missing, empty, or unparseable.

features.name: all_comments_only_abstract_normative
features.definition: All counter-argument comments in OC_comments: rely solely on abstract normative principles (values, rights, fairness, ethics, should/ought) with no concrete labor-process or personal experiential detail
features.spec: Read the JSON list in OC_comments (comments by users other than OP). Return 1 if every comment argues solely through abstract normative principles (e.g. rights, fairness, morality, what should be) and none supplies concrete personal or specific factual/process examples. Return 0 if any comment includes concrete examples, personal experience, or empirical/process detail of any kind. Return null if OC_comments is missing, empty, or unparseable. By construction this cannot be 1 when any_comment_personal_labor_process_detail is 1.

decomposed.h0: View-change rate is the same for discussions with any_comment_personal_labor_process_detail=1 as for those with all_comments_only_abstract_normative=1.
decomposed.h1: View-change rate is higher when any_comment_personal_labor_process_detail=1 than when all_comments_only_abstract_normative=1.
decomposed.note: Claim contrasts labor-detail discussions (A) with solely-abstract-normative ones (B); the reference category in the model is neither (concrete but non-labor comments), so no single coefficient is the A-vs-B contrast (it is beta_A - beta_B, a linear combination), hence term=null. Fitting A alone would compare A vs not-A, which is not the claim. 'Personal' and 'labor-process' boundaries are semantic and unspecified further. Associational only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly quantify systemic material harms to third parties rather than asserting propositional falsity are associated with a higher likelihood of view change.

features.name: any_comment_quantifies_systemic_third_party_harm
features.definition: Any counter-argument comment (OC_comments): explicitly quantifies systemic material harm to third parties (1) vs not (0)
features.spec: Read title and argument for the OP's view, then every comment in the OC_comments JSON list (ignore list order; do not use conversation). Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly gives quantities (numbers, rates, counts, amounts, percentages, or concrete magnitudes such as deaths, costs, income loss, people affected) describing systemic/structural material harm (e.g. economic, health, physical, resource harms from policies, institutions or widespread practices) borne by third parties (people other than the OP and the commenter). Qualitative harm claims without any quantification, quantified non-harm facts, and harms only to the commenter/OP do not count. Quotes of others' text inside a comment count only if the commenter adopts them. Return 0 if comments are parseable and none qualify. Return null if OC_comments is missing, empty or unparseable.

features.name: any_comment_asserts_propositional_falsity
features.definition: Any counter-argument comment (OC_comments): asserts that the OP's claim or a premise is factually or logically false (1) vs not (0)
features.spec: Read title and argument for the OP's view, then every comment in the OC_comments JSON list (ignore order; do not use conversation). Return 1 if at least one comment asserts that the OP's claim or a stated premise is false, incorrect, or logically invalid as a proposition (e.g. disputing facts, definitions or inference), as opposed to presenting harms. A comment may satisfy both this and the harm-quantification feature. Return 0 if comments are parseable and none do so. Return null if OC_comments is missing, empty or unparseable.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_quantifies_systemic_third_party_harm has no association with delta, holding any_comment_asserts_propositional_falsity fixed.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_quantifies_systemic_third_party_harm=1 have higher likelihood of delta than otherwise, holding any_comment_asserts_propositional_falsity fixed.
decomposed.note: "Rather than" implies a contrast between harm-quantifying and falsity-asserting discussions; the additive model tests the harm coefficient adjusted for falsity, not a strict harm-only vs falsity-only comparison (overlap allowed). "Any" used since no frequency rule is stated. Comment order/chronology unknown; OLS on binary outcome (linear probability).

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments identify logical contradictions within the original post's own stated premises are associated with higher view-change rates than those citing external evidence.

features.name: any_comment_identifies_internal_contradiction
features.definition: Any OC comment: points out a logical contradiction/inconsistency among the OP's own stated premises (title+argument)
features.spec: Read title, argument (OP's post) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users; order not meaningful) jointly. Output 1 if at least one comment argues that the OP's own stated premises or claims in the title/argument contradict each other or are mutually inconsistent (internal logical contradiction, using the OP's own statements). Output 0 if no comment does so (e.g., comments only disagree, give counterexamples, or cite outside facts). Do not use the conversation column. Null if OC_comments or title/argument is missing/unparseable or the list is empty. Merely mentioning the topic or disagreeing is not enough; external evidence alone does not count.

features.name: any_comment_cites_external_evidence
features.definition: Any OC comment: cites external evidence (data, studies, statistics, documented facts, or sourced real-world examples) to counter the OP
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users; order not meaningful). Output 1 if at least one comment cites evidence external to the OP's post, such as studies, statistics, data, links/sources, or documented specific facts/real-world examples, in support of a counter-argument. Output 0 if none does. Do not use the conversation column. Null if OC_comments is missing/unparseable or empty. Pure internal-logic critiques of the OP's premises without outside evidence do not count.

decomposed.h0: Discussion view-change rate (delta) does not differ with any_comment_identifies_internal_contradiction, holding any_comment_cites_external_evidence fixed.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_identifies_internal_contradiction=1 have a higher view-change rate than those with any_comment_cites_external_evidence=1 (coefficient on contradiction greater than on evidence).
decomposed.note: The claim compares contradiction-type vs evidence-type discussions, i.e. beta_contradiction minus beta_evidence. No single design-matrix coefficient represents that difference, so term is null. A linear-combination test would be needed. The two features are not mutually exclusive, so overlap is allowed. Evidence-citing is defined broadly. The comparison group is not "no contradiction". Comments are unordered, and the OP's argument may contain later edits.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments provide specific factual data or verifiable citations are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: any_comment_specific_factual_data_or_citation
features.definition: Counter-argument comments in OC_comments (not OP, not conversation replies): 1 if any comment provides specific factual data or a verifiable citation, else 0
features.spec: Read the JSON list in OC_comments (comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment provides specific factual data (e.g., concrete statistics, figures, dates, named studies, named documented events or sources) or a verifiable citation (link, named publication/author/study/law/court case that could be checked). Vague generalities, opinions, hypotheticals, anecdotes without checkable specifics, and bare assertions without specifics do not count. Quoted text from the OP does not count. Return 0 if the list is parsed and no comment qualifies. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable, or empty. Do not use the conversation column or any outcome.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_specific_factual_data_or_citation has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view.
decomposed.h1: any_comment_specific_factual_data_or_citation is positively associated with the probability that the OP changed their view.
decomposed.note: Hypothesis does not specify any/share/count; "any comment" chosen as the literal reading of "discussions where counter-arguments provide". OC_comments order carries no chronology; association only, no causal claim. Linear probability model on binary outcome.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains explicit polite apology phrases are associated with a lower likelihood of view change compared to arguments without such phrases.

features.name: op_argument_has_polite_apology
features.definition: OP's own argument text (post body only): 1 if it contains an explicit polite apology phrase, else 0
features.spec: Read only the argument column (OP's post body, which may include later edits; do not infer an original snapshot). Return 1 if the OP's own text contains at least one explicit polite apology phrase directed at readers, e.g. 'sorry', 'I apologize', 'apologies for', 'excuse my', 'pardon my', 'my bad'. Count it only when used as an apology/politeness expression by the OP. Exclude quoted text from others, apologies that are only the topic being discussed (e.g. a country apologizing), and non-apology uses of 'sorry' (e.g. 'sorry state of affairs'). Return 0 if the text is assessable and has no such phrase. Return null if argument is missing or empty/unparseable. Do not use other columns.

decomposed.h0: op_argument_has_polite_apology has no association with the likelihood of view change.
decomposed.h1: Arguments with op_argument_has_polite_apology=1 have a lower likelihood of view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Argument may contain later edits, so apologies may not be in the initial post. Phrase list is illustrative; judgment is semantic. OLS on binary outcome is a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Original posts featuring first-person vulnerable admissions are associated with higher view-change likelihood than those containing distant, third-person observations.

features.name: op_first_person_vulnerable_admission
features.definition: OP's own title and post body (excluding quoted others' text and edits-marked additions not by OP is not applicable; use OP's own words): 1 if OP makes at least one first-person vulnerable admission, else 0
features.spec: Read title and argument together. Return 1 if the OP, in their own words, makes at least one first-person vulnerable admission about themselves: e.g. admitting a personal weakness, fear, shame, mistake, insecurity, emotional struggle, or personal hardship, or openly disclosing a painful/embarrassing personal experience. Mere first-person opinions ('I think'), neutral autobiographical facts, or hedging about the argument do not count. Exclude text quoted from other people and quoted material. Marked edits in argument are part of the current text; count them only if they are the OP's own words (do not infer an initial snapshot). Return 0 if text is present and has no such admission. Return null if both title and argument are missing or unparseable. Empty argument with a non-vulnerable title gives 0.

features.name: op_distant_third_person_observation
features.definition: OP's own title and post body: 1 if OP presents distant, detached third-person observations about others/world/society, else 0
features.spec: Read title and argument together. Return 1 if the OP's post contains at least one distant third-person observation: a detached statement or observation about other people, groups, institutions, or the world (e.g. 'countries exploit groups', 'people tend to...') presented from an external, impersonal vantage without the OP personally involved. First-person personal experience or disclosure does not count as distant observation. Exclude quoted text from others. Return 0 if text is present but has none. Return null if both title and argument are missing or unparseable. This is assessed independently of the vulnerable-admission feature; a post may be 1 on both.

decomposed.h0: View-change likelihood does not differ between posts with op_first_person_vulnerable_admission and posts with op_distant_third_person_observation.
decomposed.h1: Posts featuring op_first_person_vulnerable_admission have higher view-change likelihood than posts containing op_distant_third_person_observation.
decomposed.note: The claim is a contrast between two named groups (vulnerable-admission vs distant-observation posts), i.e. beta_A - beta_B, which is not a single design-matrix coefficient in this rhs; groups may overlap, so no single term is faithful (a linear-combination test would be needed). Not substituting vulnerable vs not-vulnerable. Outcome is binary delta modeled via OLS (linear probability). Edits in argument may be later than initial post; no initial snapshot inferred.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments include direct URLs or external links are associated with a higher likelihood of view change than those solely using internal text.

features.name: any_comment_has_external_link
features.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: contains at least one direct URL or external hyperlink (1) vs none (0)
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of strings. If unparseable or missing, return null. If parsed list is empty, return null. Otherwise return 1 if any comment matches regex r'(https?://|www\.)\S+' or a markdown link of the form [text](http...), case-insensitive; else 0. Quoted text still counts since the URL itself is the measured item. Only OC_comments is read; OP text and conversation are ignored.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with any_comment_has_external_link=1 have the same likelihood of view change as those with 0.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_has_external_link=1 have a higher likelihood of view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Comparison group is "no URL in any supplied comment", treated as solely internal text; comments may still cite external sources without URLs. OC_comments may not include all comments in the discussion. No controls added.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments employ specific, verifiable procedural examples are associated with higher original post view-change rates than those relying solely on abstract theoretical rebuttals.

features.name: any_comment_specific_verifiable_procedural_example
features.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: cites at least one specific, verifiable procedural example (a concrete named or checkable process, rule, procedure, case or step-by-step mechanism of how something is actually done)
features.spec: Read the OC_comments JSON list (comments by users other than the OP; order carries no meaning). Return 1 if at least one comment gives a specific, verifiable procedural example: a concrete, checkable description of how a particular process, legal/institutional procedure, protocol, rule or workflow actually operates or operated (e.g. a named statute's steps, a specific court procedure, a documented practice), that could be checked against an external source. Generic hypotheticals, abstract principles, vague appeals to 'how things work', and personal opinions without a checkable procedure do not count. Quoted OP text does not count. Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none contain such an example. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable or empty.

features.name: all_comments_solely_abstract_theoretical_rebuttal
features.definition: All counter-argument comments in OC_comments: rebut using only abstract or theoretical reasoning, with no specific concrete verifiable example of any kind
features.spec: Read the OC_comments JSON list (comments by others than the OP). Return 1 if every comment rebuts the OP's view solely through abstract, theoretical, conceptual or principle-based reasoning, and no comment includes a specific concrete example (procedural, factual, case-based or statistical) that could be verified. Return 0 if at least one comment includes any specific concrete verifiable example. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable or empty.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with any_comment_specific_verifiable_procedural_example=1 have the same view-change rate as those with all_comments_solely_abstract_theoretical_rebuttal=1, other things equal.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_specific_verifiable_procedural_example=1 have a higher view-change rate than those with all_comments_solely_abstract_theoretical_rebuttal=1.
decomposed.note: The two indicators are nearly complementary; the residual reference group is discussions with non-procedural concrete examples only. The procedural coefficient is therefore a contrast against that reference, not exactly against abstract-only; the true contrast is beta_procedural - beta_abstract_only, which is not a single coefficient. Better tested by a subset restricted to the two named groups, which the single-feature OLS contract cannot express. 'Higher' has no threshold; 'solely' is operationalized across all comments.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains specific counter-question markers are associated with a higher probability of view change.

features.name: op_argument_has_counter_question
features.definition: OP's own argument text (excluding quoted external text and marked edits): 1 if it contains at least one explicit question posed to readers/challengers asking for counter-arguments, rebuttals or counterexamples, else 0
features.spec: Read only the argument column (OP post body). Return 1 if the OP's own text contains at least one explicit question addressed to readers/respondents that solicits a counter-argument, rebuttal, counterexample or challenge to the OP's view (e.g. 'What am I missing?', 'Can anyone give a counterexample?', 'How would you argue against this?'). Interpretation of 'counter-question markers' is this operational one. Do not count: questions inside quoted external text, rhetorical questions that are not soliciting counters, merely descriptive or topical questions, and text in marked edits/later additions (EDIT/Update sections). A bare question mark alone is not sufficient. Return 0 if the text is assessable and has no such question. Return null if argument is missing or empty/unparseable. Do not use any other columns.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with op_argument_has_counter_question=1 have the same probability of view change as those with 0.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with op_argument_has_counter_question=1 have a higher probability of view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: "Specific counter-question markers" is undefined in the hypothesis; the operational definition (OP questions soliciting counter-arguments) is an interpretation. Argument may contain later edits; these are excluded where marked, but the initial snapshot cannot be guaranteed. OLS on binary outcome is a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original poster's argument includes personal anecdotes or first-person experiential narratives are associated with a lower likelihood of view change.

features.name: op_has_personal_anecdote
features.definition: OP's own argument text (post body): 1 if it includes a personal anecdote or first-person experiential narrative about the OP's own experiences, else 0
features.spec: Read only the argument column (OP post body; may contain later edits, which cannot be separated, so judge the text as given). Return 1 if the OP recounts a personal anecdote or first-person experiential narrative about events or experiences they themselves lived (e.g., 'when I worked at...', 'my friend and I experienced...' as lived by OP). Return 0 if the text contains only abstract claims, hypotheticals, general statistics, or others' experiences with no OP personal experience. Exclude quoted external text, and mere opinion statements like 'I think' without an experience. Null if argument is missing or unparseable; empty text gives null.

decomposed.h0: op_has_personal_anecdote has no association with the likelihood of view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: op_has_personal_anecdote is associated with a lower likelihood of view change (delta).
decomposed.note: The argument may contain later edits; the initial post cannot be isolated. Linear probability model on a binary outcome; no controls specified.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly acknowledge the validity of the original post's initial premise before introducing divergence are associated with a higher likelihood of view change.

features.name: any_comment_acknowledges_op_premise_before_diverging
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments) judged against the OP title/argument: 1 if any comment explicitly acknowledges validity of the OP's premise and then introduces disagreement or divergence within that same comment.
features.spec: Read title, argument and OC_comments jointly. OC_comments is a JSON list of comments by users other than the OP; order is not chronology. Identify the OP's main/initial premise from title and argument (argument may contain later edits; do not infer an initial snapshot, use the premise as stated). Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly states that the OP's premise (or a clearly identified core premise of the OP's view) is valid, correct, reasonable or true (e.g. 'you're right that...', 'your historical analysis is not wrong'), and THEN, in the same comment, introduces a point of divergence, disagreement or counter-claim. Acknowledgement must be explicit and about the OP's premise, not mere politeness, thanks, or restating the OP's view, and not acknowledgement of a side point. Quoted text from others and moderator/bot notices do not count. Return 0 if the comments are parsed and no comment does this. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable, or title/argument are missing; an empty comment list gives 0 only if the list parses as empty.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_acknowledges_op_premise_before_diverging is unrelated to the probability of view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Rows where any_comment_acknowledges_op_premise_before_diverging is 1 have a higher probability of view change.
decomposed.note: Hypothesis says "counter-arguments" without specifying any vs. share vs. frequency; "any comment" is chosen as the minimal reading. OC_comments is unordered and argument may be edited, so the "initial" premise is approximated by the premise as stated in title/argument. Linear probability model via OLS on binary outcome; no controls.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments employ concrete personal anecdotes are more likely associated with the original poster changing their view than those using abstract reasoning.

features.name: any_comment_personal_anecdote
features.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: relates a concrete personal anecdote (commenter's own specific lived experience or event) as part of its argument.
features.spec: Read the OC_comments JSON list (comments by users other than the OP; order carries no meaning). Return 1 if at least one comment's own text recounts a concrete personal anecdote: a specific experience, event or situation that the commenter (or someone they personally know, stated as first-hand) lived through, e.g. 'when I worked at X, ...'. Generic hypotheticals, statistics, general facts, others' reported studies, quotations of the OP, and hypothetical 'imagine' scenarios do not count. Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none has such an anecdote. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable or an empty list. Do not use any other column.

features.name: any_comment_abstract_reasoning
features.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: argues through abstract reasoning (general principles, logic, definitions, or impersonal evidence) rather than concrete personal experience.
features.spec: Read the OC_comments JSON list (order meaningless). Return 1 if at least one comment's own text makes its case through abstract reasoning: general principles, logical argument, definitions, conceptual distinctions or impersonal general claims, without relying on the commenter's personal anecdote for that argument. Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none contains such reasoning (e.g. only anecdotes or non-argument text). Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable or empty. Do not use any other column. A row may be 1 on both this and any_comment_personal_anecdote.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with any_comment_personal_anecdote=1 have the same probability/mean of delta as those with it 0, holding any_comment_abstract_reasoning fixed.
decomposed.h1: any_comment_personal_anecdote is associated with a higher likelihood of OP view change, relative to abstract reasoning.
decomposed.note: The claim contrasts anecdote vs abstract reasoning groups, but the two are not mutually exclusive in a row; the coefficient is an approximation of the contrast, not a strict anecdote-only vs abstract-only comparison. Frequency/dominance of each style is unspecified (any-comment used). Discussion-level association only; OLS on binary outcome (linear probability).

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing at least three distinct counter-argument comments are associated with a higher probability of the original poster changing their view than those with fewer.

features.name: oc_comment_count
features.definition: Row's OC_comments JSON list: number of list elements (comments by users other than OP)
features.spec: import json; lst=json.loads(row['OC_comments']); n=len(lst) if isinstance(lst,list) else None. Return n (integer >=0). Return null if OC_comments is missing or unparseable; empty list gives 0. Counts list entries (comments), without semantic deduplication; list order is irrelevant.

features.name: has_three_or_more_oc_comments
features.definition: Row's OC_comments list: 1 if it contains at least 3 comments, else 0
features.spec: Using oc_comment_count: return null if it is null; 1 if oc_comment_count >= 3 else 0.

decomposed.h0: Probability of OP delta does not differ between discussions with has_three_or_more_oc_comments=1 and 0.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with has_three_or_more_oc_comments=1 have higher probability of OP view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: "Distinct" is operationalized as separate entries in OC_comments; no semantic deduplication of arguments. The list may be a subset of all comments in the discussion (dataset-constructed). Observed counts: min 1, median 1, so the fewer-than-3 group is 1-2 comments.

decomposed.hypothesis: Posts containing direct counterarguments are more likely to result in the original poster upvoting the reply or changing their view.

features.name: any_direct_counterargument
features.definition: Other users' comments in OC_comments, read against the OP title/argument: 1 if any comment directly counterargues the OP's stated view, else 0.
features.spec: Read title, argument and every comment in the OC_comments JSON list together. Return 1 if at least one comment directly counterargues the OP's view: it explicitly opposes, rebuts, or gives reasons or evidence against a specific claim or conclusion in the title/argument. Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none do so (e.g. only questions, clarification requests, agreement, jokes, off-topic, moderator/bot notices). Do not use the conversation column or any later replies. Quoted text from others does not count unless the comment itself rebuts it. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable or empty, or if title and argument are both missing.

decomposed.h0: any_direct_counterargument has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Posts with any_direct_counterargument=1 have a higher probability of the OP changing their view than posts with 0.
decomposed.note: The hypothesis also mentions the OP upvoting the reply, but no upvote data exists, so only the view-change outcome (delta) is testable. Every post in the dataset has at least one comment, so the feature may have little variance. "Direct" is operationalized as explicit rebuttal of a specific OP claim. OC_comments order carries no chronology.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument employs modest or uncertain epistemic markers are associated with a higher likelihood of view change than those using high-modality assertions.

features.name: op_modest_uncertain_epistemic_markers
features.definition: OP's own argument text (post body, excluding quoted external text and marked edits): 1 if the OP's stance is predominantly expressed with modest/uncertain epistemic markers, else 0
features.spec: Read only the argument column. Judge the OP's own claims about their view; ignore quoted external text and edit notes (e.g., 'EDIT:'). Return 1 if the OP's central claims are mainly framed with modest, hedged or uncertain epistemic markers (e.g., 'I think', 'maybe', 'might', 'perhaps', 'I'm not sure', 'it seems', 'to my knowledge', 'could be wrong'). Return 0 if the central claims are mainly stated assertively or with high-modality markers (e.g., 'definitely', 'must', 'obviously', 'always', 'undeniably', 'objectively'), or unmarked flat assertions with no hedging. If mixed, choose by how the main thesis is framed. Return null if argument is missing, empty or unparseable. Not an validated scale; no frequency cutoff is imposed beyond the predominant framing of the main thesis.

features.name: op_high_modality_assertions
features.definition: OP's own argument text (excluding quoted external text and marked edits): 1 if the OP's central claims are predominantly expressed with high-modality/certainty markers, else 0
features.spec: Read only the argument column. Judge the OP's own claims; ignore quoted external text and edit notes. Return 1 if the main thesis is mainly framed with strong certainty/high-modality markers (e.g., 'definitely', 'must', 'clearly', 'obviously', 'always', 'never', 'undeniably', 'objectively', 'there is no way'). Return 0 if the main thesis is mainly hedged/uncertain or neutrally stated without strong certainty markers. Return null if argument is missing, empty or unparseable.

decomposed.h0: op_modest_uncertain_epistemic_markers has no association with the likelihood of view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Higher op_modest_uncertain_epistemic_markers is associated with a higher likelihood of view change (delta) than op_high_modality_assertions-style framing.
decomposed.note: The two features are not exact complements (neutral unhedged text is 0 on both), so the single-coefficient test compares hedged vs not-hedged, which includes neutral posts, rather than strictly hedged vs high-modality. Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly names a specific external program (e.g. a named government/social/educational/policy program, initiative or software program) or a specific named location (e.g. a named country, city, state, region, landmark, institution site) and uses it as an example, evidence or comparison. Generic unnamed references (e.g. 'some countries', 'a program') do not count. Names appearing only inside quoted OP text do not count; names in a comment's own text count. Return 0 if all comments were readable and none does so. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable or the list is empty. List order is irrelevant. Do not use conversation or any outcome.

features.name: only_abstract_logical_refutation
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments, all comments): 1 if every comment relies solely on abstract logical refutation with no named specific external program or location, else 0
features.spec: Read OC_comments (list of comments by users other than the OP) with title and argument as context. Return 1 if every comment argues only through abstract reasoning/logical refutation (principles, definitions, logical inconsistencies, hypotheticals without named specifics) and none names a specific external program or location. Return 0 if any comment names a specific external program or location, or any comment relies on something other than abstract logical argument as its substantive content (e.g. concrete personal anecdote, statistics, named examples). Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable or empty. Do not use conversation or any outcome.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with any_comment_names_specific_external_program_or_location=1 have the same view-change rate as other discussions.

The 'not named' baseline in the regression also includes discussions that use non-named concrete content (anecdotes, statistics), so the coefficient is an approximation. A faithful test would restrict to rows where either feature is 1, and the rhs cannot subset rows. only_abstract_logical_refutation is defined for that restriction. Comment text only; no chronology is available.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly quote and refute specific phrases from the original post are associated with a higher likelihood of view change.

features.name: any_comment_quotes_and_refutes_op_phrase
features.definition: Any counter-argument comment (OC_comments): explicitly quotes a specific word/phrase/sentence from the OP's title or argument AND argues against/refutes that quoted text.
features.spec: Read title, argument (OP post) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users; order carries no chronology/rank) jointly. Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly quotes (quotation marks, blockquote '>' or clearly verbatim reproduction) a specific phrase or sentence that actually appears in the OP's title or argument, and that same comment disputes, rebuts or argues against the quoted text. Quote of text not in the OP post (e.g., another commenter), quotes only agreed with, or mere topic mentions/paraphrases without verbatim quoting give no qualification. Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none qualifies. Return null if OC_comments or the OP text is missing, empty or unparseable. Do not use conversation or any outcome information; note argument may include later edits and no initial snapshot is inferred.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_quotes_and_refutes_op_phrase has no association with the probability of view change (delta).

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly refute specific examples or anecdotes provided by the original poster are associated with a higher probability of view change compared to arguments addressing the main premise directly.

features.name: any_comment_refutes_op_example
features.definition: Any OC comment: explicitly refutes or disputes a specific example, anecdote or personal experience given by the OP in the argument text (1/0)
features.spec: Read argument (OP post body, with title not needed) and OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments; order carries no meaning) jointly. Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly argues against, rebuts or discredits a specific example, anecdote or personal experience that the OP presented in argument (e.g., disputes its facts, representativeness or interpretation). Merely mentioning the topic of the example, or agreeing with or adding new examples, does not count. Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none does this. Return null if OC_comments or argument is missing/unparseable or the list is empty. Do not use conversation or any outcome.

features.name: any_comment_addresses_main_premise
features.definition: Any OC comment: directly challenges the OP's main premise/central claim (title/argument thesis) rather than only a specific example (1/0)
features.spec: Read title, argument and OC_comments (JSON list; order meaningless) jointly. Return 1 if at least one comment directly argues against the OP's central claim or main premise as stated in title/argument (general reasoning against the thesis itself, not only rebutting a specific example or anecdote). Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none does this. Return null if title, argument or OC_comments is missing/unparseable or the list is empty. Do not use conversation or any outcome.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with any_comment_refutes_op_example=1 have the same view-change probability as those with any_comment_addresses_main_premise=1.

Neither single coefficient equals the difference beta_A - beta_B, so no single available term tests it; the two features are not mutually exclusive and can co-occur in a discussion. Comments are unordered, so no chronology is implied. Outcome is binary but fit by OLS (linear probability).

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument uses hedging or qualifying language are associated with a higher likelihood of view change than those using absolute declarative statements.

features.name: op_uses_hedging_language
features.definition: OP's own argument text (post body): 1 if it contains hedging or qualifying language about its own claims, else 0.
features.spec: Read the argument column only (OP's post body; may include later edits, which are not separated out; do not infer an initial version). Return 1 if the OP in their own voice uses at least one hedging or qualifying expression that softens or limits their own claim (e.g., 'I think maybe', 'might', 'perhaps', 'in some cases', 'generally', 'mostly', 'to my knowledge', 'I could be wrong', 'it seems'). Exclude hedges inside quoted text from others, quoted opponents, and edit notes/moderator notices not stating the OP's stance. Do not count purely generic 'I think/I believe' framing as a hedge unless it expresses uncertainty or limits scope. Return 0 if the argument is readable and contains no such hedging. Return null if argument is missing, empty, or unparseable.

features.name: op_uses_absolute_declarative_language
features.definition: OP's own argument text (post body): 1 if its central claims are stated as absolute declaratives without hedging or qualification, else 0.
features.spec: Read the argument column only (do not infer an initial version before edits). Return 1 if the OP in their own voice states their main view as an absolute, unqualified declarative (e.g., 'always', 'never', 'all', 'obviously', 'is simply', 'no exceptions') and the argument contains no hedging or qualifying language about that main claim. Return 0 if the main claim is hedged/qualified or is not stated absolutely. Exclude quoted others' text and moderator notices. Return null if argument is missing, empty, or unparseable.

decomposed.h0: Discussions whose OP argument has op_uses_hedging_language=1 have the same likelihood of view change as those with op_uses_absolute_declarative_language=1, holding the other indicator in the model.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with op_uses_hedging_language=1 have a higher likelihood of view change than discussions with op_uses_absolute_declarative_language=1.
decomposed.note: Hedging and absolute indicators are not complements and can both be 0, so the hedging coefficient is relative to neither-group posts, not a direct hedging-vs-absolute contrast. The argument may contain later edits; initial-post wording cannot be recovered. No intensity or frequency cutoff for hedging is specified. OLS on binary outcome is a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly quote the original poster's text rather than paraphrasing are associated with a higher probability of view change.

features.name: any_comment_quotes_op_text
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments): 1 if any comment explicitly quotes verbatim text from the OP's title or argument, else 0
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP) jointly with the OP title and argument. Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly quotes the OP's text verbatim or near-verbatim (e.g., Reddit '>' blockquote or quotation marks reproducing a phrase/sentence from the title or argument). Endorsement is not required; the quote may be followed by rebuttal or agreement. Paraphrases, topic mentions, and quotes of other commenters or external sources do not count. Quote must match OP text (title or argument), judged against the supplied argument, which may include later edits. Return 0 if comments are parseable and none contain such quotes. Return null if OC_comments is missing/unparseable, or title and argument are both missing. An empty comment list gives 0.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_quotes_op_text is unassociated with the probability of view change (delta).

Argument may contain later edits, so quote matching is against current text. Uses OLS (linear probability) as required.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing counter-arguments that explicitly validate the original poster's emotional experience prior to logical rebuttal are associated with higher view-change rates.

features.name: any_comment_validates_op_emotion_before_rebuttal
features.definition: Any OC comment (other users): explicitly acknowledges/validates the OP's stated emotional experience in the comment text before that same comment's logical rebuttal begins
