Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly validates the OP's emotional experience (e.g. says OP's feelings/frustration/pain are understandable, valid, legitimate, or expresses empathy for what OP felt) AND this validation appears earlier in that same comment than its counter-argument/rebuttal. Generic politeness, praise, or mere agreement with OP's facts is not validation; validation of emotions not expressed by OP, or quoted from others, does not count. Validation appearing only after the rebuttal begins does not count. Return 0 if comments are parseable and none qualify (including OP expressing no emotion). Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable, or argument/title missing. Empty comment list gives 0. Do not use conversation or any outcome information.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_validates_op_emotion_before_rebuttal has no association with delta (view-change rate).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_validates_op_emotion_before_rebuttal = 1 have a higher view-change rate than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Linear probability model on binary delta. Order within a single comment is used for "prior to rebuttal"; list order across comments is not chronology. Association only, no causal claim. Emotional experience is only assessable if OP expresses it.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing counter-arguments that use analogies to familiar scenarios are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: any_comment_uses_analogy_to_familiar_scenario
features.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: uses an analogy comparing the OP's issue to a different, familiar/everyday scenario (1) else 0
features.spec: Read the JSON list in OC_comments (comments by users other than OP; order carries no meaning). Return 1 if at least one comment itself makes an analogy, i.e. explicitly or implicitly compares the issue under debate to a different, familiar or commonly understood scenario (everyday situation, common practice, well-known case) to support its point. Count the comment's own analogy even if it is not endorsed elsewhere; exclude merely literal examples of the same issue, quoted OP text, and mere topic mentions. Return 0 if all comments are parseable and none contains such an analogy. Return null if OC_comments is missing, empty-unparseable, or not a JSON list. An empty valid list gives 0. decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_uses_analogy_to_familiar_scenario=1 have a higher likelihood of OP view change than those with 0.

features.name: title_absolute_universal_quantifier
features.definition: OP title: 1 if it explicitly contains an absolute universal quantifier/term (e.g. all, every, always, never, none, no one, nobody, everyone) used as a quantifier or frequency claim, else 0
features.spec: Read only the title. Return 1 if the title explicitly contains an absolute universal quantifier or absolute frequency term (e.g. 'all', 'every', 'everyone', 'always', 'never', 'none', 'no one', 'nobody', 'nothing') functioning as a quantifier/frequency claim over the claim's subject. Words must be literally present; do not infer implied universality from bare plurals. Ignore the 'CMV:' prefix. Return 0 if no such term is present. Return null if title is missing or empty. Do not use other columns.

features.name: title_variable_probabilistic_term
features.definition: OP title: 1 if it explicitly contains a variable or probabilistic/hedging quantifier term (e.g. some, many, most, often, sometimes, usually, generally, likely, probably, might, may, can, almost always), else 0
features.spec: Read only the title. Return 1 if the title explicitly contains a variable, partial or probabilistic quantifier/frequency/modality term (e.g. 'some', 'many', 'most', 'often', 'sometimes', 'usually', 'generally', 'rarely', 'likely', 'probably', 'might', 'may', 'could', 'almost always', 'almost never', 'tend to') used to qualify the claim. Terms must be literally present. Ignore the 'CMV:' prefix. Return 0 if none present. Return null if title is missing or empty. Do not use other columns.

features.definition: OP title: 1 if absolute-universal-only, 0 if variable/probabilistic-only, null if both or neither
features.spec: Using features a=title_absolute_universal_quantifier and p=title_variable_probabilistic_term: return 1 if a==1 and p==0; 0 if a==0 and p==1; null if a and p are both 1, both 0, or either is null. Rows with null are excluded from the test.

decomposed.note: Comparison is absolute-only vs probabilistic-only titles; titles with neither or both are excluded (null), so the sample may be small. Term lists are illustrative; ambiguity of modal words like 'can' is a limitation. Titles only, no comment text.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing counter-arguments that explicitly reference specific, concrete examples or real-world instances in the provided comments are associated with a higher probability of view change.

Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none do this. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable, or an empty list. Do not use any other column.

decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_cites_specific_example=1 have a higher probability of view change than those with 0.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments contain specific empirical evidence are more likely to be associated with the original poster changing their view than those containing only logical refutations.

features.name: any_comment_specific_empirical_evidence
features.definition: Any OC comment: asserts specific empirical evidence (e.g. named study, statistic, data, documented historical/real-world case or source) in support of its argument, 1 if at least one comment does

Acknowledgment must come before the counter-example in the comment text. Exclude quoted text from others, reported positions not adopted by the commenter, and bot/moderator notices. Return 0 if the comments are assessable and no comment meets both conditions. Return null if OC_comments is missing/unparseable or title/argument is missing; an empty list gives 0. decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments utilize second-person direct address are associated with higher original poster view-change rates than arguments relying on third-person analysis.

features.name: any_comment_second_person_address
features.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: 1 if at least one comment's own text uses second-person direct address toward the OP or reader (you/your/you're/yourself) in its argumentation.

Return 0 if the list parses and has comments but none has such address. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable, or an empty list. Do not use order or any other column.

features.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: 1 if at least one comment's argument is framed as third-person analysis (about people, groups, things, or the issue in general) rather than by addressing the OP directly.

Return 1 if at least one comment relies mainly on third-person analysis: it argues about the topic, people, groups, institutions, or evidence using third-person framing (he/she/they/it/people/names/the issue) without relying on direct address of the OP/reader as its main mode. Exclude quoted external text and bot/moderator notices. Return 0 if the list parses with comments but none is mainly third-person analysis. features.name: example_comment_count
features.definition: OC_comments (each counter-argument comment by other users): number of comments that contain at least one specific real-world example
features.spec: Read OC_comments, a JSON list of comment strings by users other than the OP. Parse it; if missing or unparseable return null. For each comment decide whether it cites at least one specific real-world example (a named or concretely identifiable real event, person, organization, place, study, law, product, or concrete real case) used to support or illustrate its point. Generic claims, hypotheticals, vague generalities ('many people'), and the commenter's unspecific personal anecdote without concrete identifiable details do not count; quotes of the OP alone do not count. Return the integer count of comments meeting this, range 0 to number of comments. An empty parsed list gives 0. Count comments, not distinct examples; do not use conversation or any other column.

decomposed.h0: Number of example_comment_count has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view.
decomposed.h1: Higher example_comment_count is associated with a higher probability that the OP changed their view.
decomposed.note: Count is raw and correlated with total number of comments (no control added, as the claim specifies none). OLS on binary outcome is a linear probability model. Specificity of examples is a semantic judgment; the anecdote boundary is operational.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments contain direct textual quotations from the original post are associated with higher view change than those avoiding explicit text reuse.

features.name: any_comment_quotes_op_text
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments, not OP): 1 if any comment contains a direct textual quotation of the OP's title or argument text, else 0
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users) jointly with title and argument (OP post). Return 1 if at least one comment directly quotes wording from the OP's title or argument: verbatim or near-verbatim text reproduced as a quotation (e.g., Reddit '>' blockquote or quotation marks) that matches the OP's text. Endorsement is not required; the commenter may quote in order to refute. Do not count mere topic mentions, paraphrases without quoted text, quotes of third parties/other sources, or quotes that do not match the OP text. Quotes of the OP in later replies in 'conversation' are not read. Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none quote the OP. Return null if OC_comments is missing/unparseable or title/argument is missing so matching cannot be assessed; an empty list gives null. Argument may include later edits; match against the supplied argument/title as given, with no inference of an initial snapshot.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_quotes_op_text is unassociated with view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_quotes_op_text = 1 have higher view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Comments are unordered and may be a subset of discussion; quote matching to the possibly edited argument; 'avoiding explicit text reuse' is operationalized as no detected quotation of OP text.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly acknowledge the original poster's validity before introducing a narrower, specific caveat are associated with higher view-change rates than those offering immediate, blanket contradictions.

features.name: any_comment_acknowledges_then_narrow_caveat
features.definition: Any OC comment: explicitly acknowledges validity of the OP's view/point (partial agreement, 'you're right that...') and only afterwards introduces a narrower, specific caveat or exception: 1 if present
features.spec: Read title and argument (for the OP's view) and the OC_comments JSON list (comments by other users; order is not chronology). Return 1 if at least one comment first explicitly acknowledges that the OP's view or a specific OP point is valid/reasonable/partly correct, and then, later in the same comment, raises a narrow, specific caveat, exception or qualification rather than a wholesale rejection. Generic politeness, praise of the post, or acknowledging only effort/tone does not count. Quoted text from others does not count unless the commenter adopts it. Return 0 if comments are assessable and none do this. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable, or empty/unassessable. Do not use conversation or later replies.

features.name: any_comment_immediate_blanket_contradiction
features.definition: Any OC comment: opens by directly contradicting/rejecting the OP's view broadly, with no prior acknowledgment of its validity: 1 if present
features.spec: Read title and argument (for the OP's view) and the OC_comments JSON list (order is not chronology). Return 1 if at least one comment immediately and wholesale contradicts or rejects the OP's view or main claim (e.g. 'No, this is wrong', sweeping denial) without first acknowledging any validity in it and without confining itself to a narrow specific caveat. Return 0 if comments are assessable and none do this. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable, or empty. Do not use conversation or later replies.

decomposed.h0: View-change rate does not differ between discussions with any_comment_acknowledges_then_narrow_caveat and those with any_comment_immediate_blanket_contradiction.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_acknowledges_then_narrow_caveat have higher view-change rates than those with any_comment_immediate_blanket_contradiction.
decomposed.note: The claim is a contrast (beta_acknowledge - beta_blanket), which is not a single design-matrix coefficient, so term is null. Individual coefficients compare each feature against its absence, not the two groups against each other. The features are not mutually exclusive across comments, since a discussion can have both. Comment order is unknown, so 'before' is judged only within a single comment. The measurement reads only OC_comments with OP context and does not use conversation.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions with post creation timestamps later in the dataset period are associated with a higher likelihood of view change.

features.name: post_creation_timestamp
features.definition: Original post: Unix creation timestamp in seconds (larger = later in dataset period).
features.spec: df['post_created_utc'] converted with pd.to_numeric(errors='coerce'); return as float seconds since epoch. Null if missing or unparseable. Observed range ~1361310562 to 1748588296, integer, no missing.

decomposed.h0: post_creation_timestamp has no association with view change (coefficient = 0).
decomposed.h1: Higher post_creation_timestamp is associated with higher likelihood of view change (coefficient > 0).
decomposed.note: Linear OLS (linear probability model) assumes a monotonic linear time trend; coefficient is per second (small in magnitude). "Dataset period" taken as the observed timestamp range. Dataset is balanced on outcome, which may affect interpretation of base rates.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing counter-arguments that explicitly quote or reference specific textual elements of the original post are associated with a higher probability of the original poster's view changing.

features.name: any_comment_quotes_or_references_op_text
features.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: explicitly quotes or specifically references an identifiable textual element of the OP's title/argument; 1 if at least one does, else 0.
features.spec: Read title, argument (OP post; may include later edits, do not treat as an initial snapshot) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users; order carries no meaning) jointly. Output 1 if at least one comment explicitly quotes (quote-formatted '>' text or quotation marks reproducing OP wording) or specifically refers to an identifiable textual element of the OP's title/argument (e.g. 'you said X', 'your second paragraph', a particular example or phrase the OP used) such that the element can be located in the OP text. Quoting need not be endorsed; the commenter may disagree. Merely addressing the general topic, generic phrases like 'your view', or quoting other commenters or external sources does not count. Output 0 if all comments are assessable and none do this. Output null if OC_comments is missing/unparseable or empty, or title and argument are both missing/empty. Do not use conversation or any outcome information.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_quotes_or_references_op_text has no association with the probability of delta (OP view change).
decomposed.h1: Rows with any_comment_quotes_or_references_op_text = 1 have a higher probability of OP view change than rows with 0.
decomposed.note: Hypothesis says "discussions containing" such comments; operationalized as any comment. OLS on binary outcome is a linear probability model. OC_comments are the supplied comments only; conversation (leaky) is not used. argument may include later edits.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the counter-arguments contain direct quotations from the original post are associated with a higher probability of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: any_comment_quotes_op_post
features.definition: Any OC_comments comment: contains a direct quotation (verbatim or near-verbatim text, e.g. in quote marks or markdown '>' block) taken from the OP's title or argument; 1 if any, else 0
features.spec: Read title, argument and the OC_comments JSON list (list of comments by users other than the OP; order carries no meaning). Return 1 if at least one comment contains a direct quotation of the OP's words, i.e. a passage reproduced verbatim or near-verbatim from the title or argument, typically marked by quotation marks or a '>' / '>' blockquote, and which matches text actually in the OP's title/argument. Endorsement is not required; the commenter may be disputing the quote. Do not count quotes from other sources, paraphrases, mere topic mentions, or quoted text that does not appear in the OP's post. Ignore the conversation column. Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none quote the OP. Return null if OC_comments is missing/unparseable or title and argument are both missing; an empty comment list gives null. Note argument may contain later edits; the quote is matched against current text.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with any_comment_quotes_op_post=1 have the same probability of OP delta as those with 0.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_quotes_op_post=1 have a higher probability of OP changing their view than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Linear probability model via OLS on binary outcome. "Contain" interpreted as any comment (not share/count). Association only; argument may include later edits so quote matching uses current text. No controls added.

decomposed.hypothesis: ChangeMyView posters receiving substantive counterarguments demonstrate higher levels of view modification than those receiving only supportive comments.

features.name: any_substantive_counterargument
features.definition: Non-OP comments in OC_comments: 1 if at least one comment presents a substantive counterargument (reasoned evidence/logic/example challenging the OP's stated view), else 0
features.spec: Read title and argument (the OP's view) and the OC_comments JSON list jointly. Return 1 if at least one comment offers a substantive counterargument to the OP's view: a reasoned challenge supported by argument, evidence, or example, not mere disagreement, insult, or a bare question. Return 0 if the list is parsed and no comment does so (e.g. all comments are supportive, off-topic, or only unsupported assertions). Ignore quoted text of others unless the commenter adopts it. Return null if OC_comments is missing/unparseable or title and argument are both missing; an empty parsed list gives null (no comments to assess). List order carries no meaning.

features.name: only_supportive_comments
features.definition: Non-OP comments in OC_comments: 1 if every comment supports/agrees with the OP's view and none challenges it, else 0
features.spec: Read title and argument (the OP's view) and the OC_comments JSON list jointly. Return 1 if all comments express support for or agreement with the OP's view (e.g. reinforcing it) and no comment challenges, disputes, or offers a counterargument to it. Return 0 if at least one comment challenges or disagrees with the view, or is neutral/not supportive. Neutral or off-topic comments mean the 'all supportive' condition fails, giving 0. Return null if OC_comments is missing/unparseable or empty, or title and argument are both missing. List order carries no meaning.

decomposed.h0: Posts with any_substantive_counterargument=1 have the same view-change rate as posts with only_supportive_comments=1.
decomposed.h1: Posts with any_substantive_counterargument=1 have a higher view-change rate than posts with only_supportive_comments=1.
decomposed.note: The claim contrasts two named groups. In the model both coefficients are relative to a residual group (neither substantive counterargument nor only supportive, e.g. neutral or unsupported comments), so no single coefficient equals the contrast; it would need a linear contrast (beta_A - beta_B), which the single-term format cannot represent. Also, all comments are by construction counter-argument comments, so the only_supportive group may be very small. The outcome delta is not used by any feature. Comments have no timestamps and list order has no meaning.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing specific counter-arguments citing empirical examples are more likely to be associated with original poster view change than those lacking such evidence.

features.name: any_comment_cites_empirical_example
features.definition: Any OC_comments comment: makes a specific counter-argument that cites a specific empirical example (concrete real-world case, event, study, statistic or data point) as evidence; 1 if any, else 0
features.spec: Read the OC_comments JSON list (comments by users other than the OP; order carries no meaning). Return 1 if at least one comment presents a counter-argument that cites a specific empirical example as evidence: a named or concretely identifiable real-world case, event, study, dataset, statistic or documented observation, used to support its point. Generic assertions, hypotheticals, personal opinion, pure logic, and vague appeals ('studies show' with no identifiable specifics) do not count. Quoted text from the OP does not count. Return 0 if the list is parseable and no comment qualifies. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable, or empty. Do not use conversation, later replies, or any outcome information.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with any_comment_cites_empirical_example=1 have the same probability of OP view change as those with 0.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_cites_empirical_example=1 have a higher probability of OP view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Associational only; OLS on binary outcome (linear probability). "Specific" and "empirical example" operationalized by the prompt rubric. Only OC_comments is read, so comments are those supplied, not necessarily the full discussion.

decomposed.hypothesis: Posts where the original poster explicitly requests emotional support or assistance in the argument text are less likely to result in a view change.

features.name: op_requests_emotional_support_or_assistance
features.definition: OP's own argument text: 1 if the OP explicitly asks readers for emotional support or for assistance (help), else 0
features.spec: Read only the argument column (OP post body, may include later edits; do not infer an initial version). Return 1 if the OP, in their own words, explicitly requests emotional support (e.g., comfort, encouragement, reassurance, sympathy) or assistance/help (e.g., 'please help me', 'I need help/support with this') from readers. Request must be explicit, not merely implied by distress or by the generic CMV invitation to change their view/argue. Exclude text quoted from others, and moderator/bot notices. Return 0 if the argument is readable and contains no such explicit request. Return null if argument is missing, empty or unparseable.

decomposed.h0: Posts with op_requests_emotional_support_or_assistance=1 have the same probability of a view change (delta) as posts with 0.
decomposed.h1: Posts with op_requests_emotional_support_or_assistance=1 have a lower probability of a view change than posts with 0.
decomposed.note: Claim joins 'emotional support or assistance' as one construct; 'assistance' is broad and may be ambiguous. The argument may include later edits, so the request is not guaranteed to be in the initial post. OLS on binary outcome is a linear probability model. Likely rare predictor.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments introduce concrete, external factual analogies are associated with higher view-change rates than those relying solely on abstract logical refutation.

features.name: any_comment_concrete_external_analogy
features.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: introduces at least one concrete, external factual analogy (a specific real-world case, event, or parallel situation outside the OP's own scenario, used as a comparison)
features.spec: Read title, argument (OP context) and the OC_comments JSON list (comments by other users; order carries no meaning). Return 1 if at least one comment itself introduces a concrete external factual analogy: a specific real-world case, event, institution, or real parallel situation outside the OP's scenario, drawn on to compare with or illuminate the OP's view. Hypotheticals that are purely invented, abstract principles, generic logic, and mere restating of OP's own examples do not count. Quotes of others do not count unless the commenter uses them as such an analogy. Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none do this. Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable, or empty. Do not use conversation or any outcome.

features.name: all_comments_abstract_logical_refutation_only
features.definition: All counter-argument comments in OC_comments: rely solely on abstract logical refutation, with no concrete external factual analogy or specific real-world example in any comment
features.spec: Read title, argument (OP context) and the OC_comments JSON list. Return 1 if every comment's counter-argument consists only of abstract reasoning (logical refutation, definitions, principle-based argument, pointing out inconsistencies) and no comment introduces any concrete external factual analogy or specific real-world case/example. Return 0 if any comment introduces a concrete external factual analogy or specific real-world example, or if some comment relies on something other than abstract logic in the stated sense (e.g. concrete evidence). Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable or empty. Do not use conversation or any outcome.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with any_comment_concrete_external_analogy=1 do not differ in view-change rate from discussions with all_comments_abstract_logical_refutation_only=1.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_concrete_external_analogy=1 have higher view-change rates than those with all_comments_abstract_logical_refutation_only=1.
decomposed.note: Claim contrasts analogy discussions with abstract-only discussions. With both indicators, the reference is neither (mostly rows with concrete non-analogy examples), and the claimed contrast is beta_analogy minus beta_abstract, not a single coefficient, so term is null. Restricting to the two groups is not expressible in the rhs. "Abstract-only" is operationalized by a prompt; no frequency cutoff is applied. Comments are only the supplied subset, with no chronology.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument exceeds one hundred words are associated with a lower likelihood of view change than shorter arguments.

features.name: argument_word_count
features.definition: OP argument (post body) text: number of whitespace-delimited words
features.spec: len(str(argument).split()) if argument is a non-null string, else null. Counts all words in the argument column as supplied (including quotes and marked edits); unit = words; empty string gives 0.

features.name: argument_over_100_words
features.definition: OP argument (post body): 1 if word count is strictly greater than 100, else 0
features.spec: Let n = len(str(argument).split()) for non-null argument; return 1 if n > 100 else 0; null if argument is missing. Exactly 100 words gives 0.

decomposed.h0: argument_over_100_words has no association with the likelihood of view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Arguments with argument_over_100_words = 1 have a lower likelihood of view change than arguments of 100 words or fewer.
decomposed.note: Word count uses whitespace splitting on the current argument text, which may include later edits and quotes; the original-at-post-time text is unavailable. Most arguments exceed 100 words (min 18, 25th percentile 177), so the short group is small. OLS on binary outcome is a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original post's argument explicitly acknowledges potential counterpoints are associated with a higher likelihood of the view changing.

features.name: op_acknowledges_counterpoints
features.definition: OP's own argument text (post body): 1 if the OP explicitly acknowledges potential counterpoints, objections or opposing considerations to their view, else 0
features.spec: Read the argument column (OP post body; may contain later marked edits, which cannot be separated, so read the whole text as given). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly acknowledges that there are potential counterpoints, objections, counterarguments, or opposing views to their position (e.g. 'some may argue', 'I know the counterargument is...', 'I can see the other side', 'one objection might be...'), including anticipating and addressing them. Return 0 if no such explicit acknowledgment exists. Do not count external quotations or other people's positions quoted without OP adopting the acknowledgment of them as counterpoints to the OP's view, mere topic mention, generic invitations to 'change my view', or general uncertainty without referencing counterpoints. Empty or missing argument: null. Output 1, 0 or null.

decomposed.h0: op_acknowledges_counterpoints has no association with the likelihood of delta (view change).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with op_acknowledges_counterpoints=1 have a higher likelihood of view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Argument may contain later edits, so acknowledgment may not be in the initial post. OLS on binary outcome is a linear probability model. Observational association only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Observed discussions with a higher log-transformed length measure are associated with a higher probability that the original poster changes their view.

features.name: log_length_measure
features.definition: Supplied log_length column: the row's numeric value as given, unchanged
features.spec: df['log_length'] converted with pd.to_numeric(errors='coerce'); return the value as float; null if missing or unparseable. No rescaling or recomputation (construction undocumented; observed range about 0.69 to 7.44).

decomposed.h0: log_length_measure has no association with the probability that the OP changes their view (coefficient = 0).
decomposed.h1: Higher log_length_measure is associated with a higher probability that the OP changes their view (coefficient > 0).

decomposed.hypothesis: Disclosures of personal emotional vulnerability in the original argument are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: op_personal_emotional_vulnerability_disclosure
features.definition: OP's own argument text: 1 if the OP discloses their own personal emotional vulnerability (e.g., own fear, shame, anxiety, depression, loneliness, hurt, insecurity, distress), else 0
features.spec: Read only the argument column (OP's post body). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, discloses a personal emotional vulnerability about themselves: e.g. admits feeling afraid, ashamed, anxious, depressed, lonely, hurt, insecure, helpless or emotionally struggling, in a way that exposes their own feelings or fragility. Edits within the argument may count if written by the OP. Return 0 if the text is assessable and contains no such disclosure; generic opinions, abstract emotional language, anger at others without vulnerability, third-party feelings, and quoted/reported others' emotions do not count, nor does merely stating a factual personal experience without emotional vulnerability. Return null if argument is missing, empty or unparseable. Do not use any other columns or infer outcomes.

decomposed.h0: op_personal_emotional_vulnerability_disclosure has no association with the probability of OP changing their view.
decomposed.h1: Posts with op_personal_emotional_vulnerability_disclosure=1 have a higher probability of OP view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Binary presence only; no intensity or frequency specified in claim. OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model. Argument may include later edits; no initial snapshot is inferable.

features.name: any_comment_specific_empirical_evidence
features.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: contains specific empirical evidence (1) vs none (0)
features.spec: Read the JSON list in OC_comments (comments by users other than the OP; order carries no meaning). Return 1 if at least one comment itself presents specific empirical evidence in support of its argument: concrete data, statistics, named studies or sources, documented historical/factual cases with verifiable particulars, or measured observations. Vague generalities, hypotheticals, pure logic, opinion, personal anecdote without verifiable particulars, and evidence only quoted from the OP do not count. Return 0 if the list is parseable and no comment qualifies. Return null if OC_comments is missing, empty, or unparseable. Do not use any other column.

features.name: any_comment_well_reasoned_counterargument
features.definition: Any OC comment (non-OP): 1 if at least one comment directly engages the OP's stated view with a well-reasoned counterargument (explicit reasons/evidence/logic linking to the OP's claim).
features.spec: Read title and argument (OP's view) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users; order is not rank/chronology). Return 1 if at least one comment presents a counterargument to the OP's view that is well-reasoned: it addresses the OP's actual claim and supports its opposing position with coherent logic, evidence or specific examples (not mere assertion, insult, joke, question-only, or off-topic). Return 0 if comments are parseable and none qualifies. Return null if OC_comments is missing/unparseable or title and argument are both missing. Empty list -> null. Do not use any other columns.

features.name: op_logical_concession_count
features.definition: OP's own statements in conversation: count of distinct logical concessions (acknowledging a counterpoint is valid/correct or partially conceding a reasoned point), excluding quoted others' text and bot notices.
features.spec: Read conversation (formatted text with speaker tags) and argument (to identify the OP's identity/context only if identifiable). Count distinct statements by the OP (only if the OP's replies are identifiable in the conversation) that concede a point on logical grounds, e.g. acknowledging an opposing argument is valid, a flaw in their own reasoning, or a fair point. Exclude quotations of others, moderator/bot notices, thanks without concession, and mere politeness. Output a non-negative integer count. 0 if the OP's replies are identifiable and none concede. Null if the OP's replies cannot be identified or conversation is missing/unparseable. The conversation column may include later replies and leakage, and OP identification may be unreliable. 'Frequency' is measured as a count with no cutoff; no frequency boundary is specified.

features.name: any_comment_cites_numerical_data
features.definition: Any counter-argument comment in OC_comments: contains specific numerical data or statistics offered as evidence (1) vs none (0)
features.spec: Read the JSON list in OC_comments (comments by users other than the OP; order carries no meaning). Quoted figures from others count if the comment uses them as evidence. Do not count vague quantifiers ('most', 'many'), numbers that are merely ordinals/list numbering, hypothetical illustrative arithmetic, or incidental numbers not serving as data (times, addresses). Return 0 if all comments are assessable and none contain such data (general assertions only). Return null if OC_comments is missing, unparseable, or empty. Do not use other columns.
